title: Farming by the Flood
objective: After this level you can describe the farming year of flood, planting and harvest.
summary: The Egyptian year had three seasons: Akhet (the flood), Peret (plowing and sowing) and Shemu (harvest and low water). Emmer wheat and barley were the main crops.

cards.headline: The Egyptian year had three seasons, and every one was about the Nile.
cards.body: Not spring, summer, autumn and winter. Flood, emergence and low water. Here’s how a farmer’s year ran on the river’s clock.

events.label: The land comes out of the water; farmers plow and sow
Harvest, then a dry spell until the next flood

cards.headline: Planting crew: sheep
cards.body: Once the flood drained off, the soil was soaked and freshly fertilized, ready for the plow. Farmers tilled it with a wooden plow pulled by an ox or a donkey. The seed went in from a funnel on the plow, or it was trodden into the soil by sheep. Yes, sheep. Some of Egypt’s planting crew walked on four legs and never asked for wages.

mascot.line: Best farmhands in Egypt: they worked for grass.

cards.headline: What grew in the mud
cards.body: The main crops were emmer wheat and six-rowed barley, with lentils, beans, onions and flax alongside. Flax mattered more than it looks: Egyptians wove it into linen. When the grain ripened, farmers cut it with sickles, then the river dropped to its lowest before rising again. One flood, one sowing, one harvest. A whole country planted in last summer’s mud.

cards.headline: The farming year: planted
learned: Three seasons: Akhet (flood), Peret (emergence), Shemu (low water)
Farmers plowed and sowed in the wet silt
Sheep sometimes trod the seed into the soil
Main crops: emmer wheat and barley; flax made linen

questions.prompt: Which season of the Egyptian year was named for the Nile’s flood?

options.label: Peret
options.rationale: Peret was when the land emerged from the flood.

options.label: Shemu
options.rationale: Shemu was the season of low water.

options.label: Kemet
options.rationale: Kemet was the black land, not a season.

questions.explanation: Akhet means the inundation, the four months when the flood covered the fields.

questions.prompt: Why did Egyptian farmers plow and sow during Peret?

options.label: It was Egypt’s rainy season
options.rationale: Egypt gets very little rain in any season.

options.label: The land had just come out of the flood, soaked and fertile
The river was at its highest point
options.rationale: At its highest, the fields were underwater.

options.label: The crops from Akhet were ready to harvest

questions.explanation: As the flood drained away, it left wet, silt-rich soil that was ready for the plow.

questions.prompt: From Level 3: in which land did Egypt’s emmer wheat and barley grow?

options.label: The oases of the Western Desert only
options.rationale: The main farmland was along the river.

options.label: Kemet, the black land of the Nile valley
The rocky banks of the First Cataract
options.rationale: The crops needed the flood’s silt.

questions.explanation: Crops grew in the narrow strip of black, silt-covered land along the Nile.
